bottlesmostly:block-handbooktext-bottles: See Meal making guide. Fill by rightmouse clicking on a cooking pot, crock, bucket, or other container with food or liquid inside (either while placed or in the inventory management screen, and also when on a shelf for meals). If you want to empty a bowl without eating the contents, simply toss it in some water!

Like ceramic crocks, calabash crocks can have portions removed or added by placing them on the ground, and then clicking on them with another container. Additionally, when on the ground crocks can be sealed by clicking on them with wax or fat. Both of these actions can also be done when the crock is on a shelf or within the inventory management screen.
bottlesmostly:survivalinfo-vessels-text:
Drinking Vessels
When playing with a thirst mechanic enabled, it is crucial to know where to find drinkable water, and to stay within reasonable distance of it while exploring, which can be quite limiting to early game exploration.
To combat this, Bottles, Mostly adds a handfull of vessels obtainable earlier than the vanilla ceramic jug, that is, pre-pottery. They are as follows:

Calabash Bottle
Calabash, or bottle gourds, are vines found in warm and temperate climates. Their fresh fruit can be used as a cooking ingredient or be left to dry. When dried, it's exterior hardens and it's interior becomes hollow, making it useful as a vessel.
One vine may produce gourds ranging in shape and size. The larger gourds can be made into crude bottles, which can later be sealed with beeswax to make a permanent vessel, and upgraded with leather, for vanity. Additionally, some gourds can be made into bowls or crocks.

Bamboo Bottle
In climates where bamboo can be found, a very simple vessel can be made from one of its segments. These bamboo bottles can't hold much liquid, however.

Waterskin
A crude vessel made from a tied up animal hide. This can be done through a rudimentary tanning method using blackcurrants or blueberries (although you will need to wait for it to cure), or with the more familiar pelts. Either way, this type of waterskin may not endure use for very long.
Once you've acquired leather, a more sophisticated waterskin can be made. It has a large, maybe unwieldy internal volume, but your animal mount should be able to handle it.
